parts.label: a
parts.reason: Impulse and momentum, direct collision problems are not mentioned in any M-section statement (M6-M9 cover kinematics, Newton's laws, friction, moments, forces - no mention of impulse, momentum, or collisions).

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Same as (a): impulse/momentum/collision concept is absent from all statements.

parts.label: (i)+(ii)
parts.technique: Equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces (resolving two strings)
parts.reason: M8.4 explicitly covers 'equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces' and resolving forces in 2 dimensions; this is a particle hanging from two strings, a standard equilibrium resolving problem.

parts.label: main
parts.technique: Connected particles via pulley on inclined plane with friction
parts.reason: M8.4 guidance explicitly states 'Problems may be set where forces need to be resolved, e.g. at least one of the particles is moving on an inclined plane' and 'application to problems involving smooth pulleys and connected particles'; friction covered by M8.6.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: suvat / motion under gravity, projectiles vertically
parts.reason: M7.3 covers suvat constant acceleration formulae and M8.3 covers motion under gravity in a straight line; this is one-dimensional vertical motion under gravity, fully covered.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Same suvat method as (a), directly covered by M7.3/M8.3; depends on part (a) answer but (a) is in spec so this is fine.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: Directly covered by M7.3 (constant acceleration formulae for straight-line motion).

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Same as (a), M7.3 covers finding acceleration from suvat.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Newton's second law on inclined plane with friction (F ≤ μR model)
parts.reason: M8.6 covers friction model F=μR for a moving body, M8.2 covers resolving on inclined plane with Newton's second law.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Vector position with constant velocity (r = r0 + vt)
parts.reason: M7.3 explicitly covers suvat in 2D with vectors, r=ut+... form applicable to constant velocity motion using vectors and i-j notation; also links to P10 vector work.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Equating vector position expressions to find meeting point/unknown component
parts.reason: Extension of same constant-velocity vector kinematics, covered by M7.3 (2D vectors, i-j form) combined with basic vector equality (P10 vectors, no dot/cross product needed).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Magnitude of position vector (distance from origin)
parts.reason: P10.2/P10.4 cover magnitude of a vector and distance calculations; straightforward within vector kinematics context of M7.3.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Newton's second law for connected particles (towbar) resolved horizontally with resistance
parts.reason: M8.4 covers connected particles (towbar analogous to pulley/lift connected particle problems) and resolving forces; guidance mentions connected particle problems including forces like resistance/tension.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Newton's second law for whole system / truck with braking force and resistance
parts.reason: Same connected-particle Newton's second law approach as (b), covered by M8.2/M8.4.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Moments of a uniform rod on two supports (equilibrium)
parts.reason: M9.1 explicitly covers 'moments in simple static contexts' including 'equilibrium of rigid bodies' - this is a standard rod-on-two-supports moments problem.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Moments of a rod with added particle mass, two supports
parts.reason: Same as (a), extension of moments on a rigid body with an added point mass, covered by M9.1.
